newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tsumura says former subsidiary declared bankrupt.
newsitem.headline: Tsumura says former subsidiary declared bankrupt.

text.p: Tsumura & Co said on Tuesday that its former subsidiary Tsumura Shoji, in which it holds a 1.66 percent stake, has been declared bankrupt.
A company spokesman said, however, that it could not confirm Tsumura Shoji's debts.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Tuesday that Tsumura Shoji had debts totaling 4.9 billion yen.
Tsumura Shoji was originally set up as a wholly owned subsidiary of Tsumura, Japan's largest maker of Chinese medicines, in 1985, the spokesman said.
